newsitem.title: MEXICO: Panamco sees further purchases this year.
newsitem.headline: Panamco sees further purchases this year.

text.p: Panamerican Beverages Inc (Panamco) said on Thursday it saw 1997 sales volumes rising in the "high single digits" and added it could make new purchases of Coca-Cola bottlers in Latin America.
In an interview with Reuters, CEO Francisco Sanchez-Loaeza said the company saw little effect on shares from the May purchase of Coca-Cola y Hit in Venezuela.

Sanchez-Loaeza said the company's sales should grow between six and nine percent in Mexico this year and about the same amount at the overall company level. "We like to say high single digits (for sales growth)," he said.
Panamco is Latin America's largest soft-drink bottler and the second largest in the world.
Sanchez-Loaeza said the company is actively seeking to expand and is currently in buyout talks with "about three or four" bottlers in the region.

"There are ongoing talks with about three or four bottlers. We never know when any of them could be completed. One has been going on for two years. But for sure we will have completed at least one before year end," he said.
Panamco exchanged 30.6 million of its shares and about $100 million in cash for Coca-Cola Hit de Venezuela, which was jointly owned by the Coca-Cola Company and the Cisneros Group of Companies.
Sanchez-Loaeza said the company is still carrying out its due diligence on the purchase and said it would have details on the financial effect of the buy when it reports second quarter profits.

"In terms of cash, the operation will be a positive for all shareholders... In including the effect from goodwill, the operation could be less accretive to shareholders," he said. "The way we have calculated our growth, the impact from goodwill will be marginal."
He added the Venezuelan and Mexican markets should both recover this year after several years of weak growth.
"We are already seeing signs of a recovery," he said.
